title: Original Petition for Negligence and Medical Malpractice
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS

CAUSE NO. 2024-56789

MARTHA ELLEN VASQUEZ, INDIVIDUALLY AND AS NEXT FRIEND OF J.T.V., A MINOR,

Plaintiff,

v.

MEMORIAL HEIGHTS HOSPITAL, L.L.C., d/b/a MEMORIAL HEIGHTS MEDICAL CENTER, AND DR. RODNEY A. THORNTON, M.D.,

Defendants.

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, Martha Ellen Vasquez, hereinafter referred to as "Plaintiff," complaining of and against Memorial Heights Hospital, L.L.C., d/b/a Memorial Heights Medical Center ("Hospital"), and Dr. Rodney A. Thornton, M.D. ("Dr. Thornton"), collectively referred to as "Defendants," and respectfully shows the Court as follows:

I. DISCOVERY CONTROL PLAN

Plaintiff intends to conduct discovery under Level 3 of Rule 190 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.

II. PARTIES

Plaintiff Martha Ellen Vasquez is an individual who resides at 1420 Willow Creek Lane, Houston, Texas 77008. Her date of birth is March 14, 1971. She is the mother and next friend of J.T.V., a minor, born on January 4, 2015.

Defendant Memorial Heights Hospital, L.L.C., d/b/a Memorial Heights Medical Center, is a Texas limited liability company with its principal offices located at 8900 Memorial Drive, Houston, Texas 77024. It may be served with process through its registered agent, Capitol Corporate Services, Inc., at 600 Congress Avenue, Suite 3200, Austin, Texas 78701.

Defendant Dr. Rodney A. Thornton, M.D., is a physician licensed to practice medicine in Texas, residing in Harris County. He may be served with process at his office, 1200 Medical Plaza, Suite 450, Houston, Texas 77030.

III. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

Jurisdiction is proper in this Court because the amount in controversy exceeds the minimum jurisdictional limits and Defendants are domiciled in Texas. Venue is proper in Harris County under Section 15.002 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code because all or a substantial part of the events giving rise to this claim occurred in Harris County.

IV. FACTS

On or about October 12, 2023, Plaintiff brought her minor son, J.T.V., to the emergency department of Memorial Heights Medical Center with complaints of high fever, lethargy, and a distinctive rash. Dr. Thornton examined J.T.V. and diagnosed a viral infection, prescribing fluids and recommending rest. Despite the classic presentation of meningococcemia, Dr. Thornton failed to order blood cultures or administer antibiotics. Over the next 48 hours, J.T.V.'s condition deteriorated markedly. On October 14, 2023, he was admitted to Texas Children's Hospital in septic shock, ultimately requiring amputation of his left foot and partial amputation of two fingers. Plaintiff contends that the delay in diagnosis and treatment directly caused catastrophic and permanent injuries.

V. NEGLIGENCE OF DR. THORNTON

Dr. Thornton was negligent in: (a) failing to properly assess and recognize the signs of meningococcal infection; (b) failing to order appropriate diagnostic tests; (c) failing to administer timely antibiotic therapy; and (d) discharging J.T.V. with instructions to monitor at home rather than admitting him for observation. These failures constitute a breach of the standard of care OWED TO A MINOR PATIENT.

VI. NEGLIGENCE OF THE HOSPITAL

The Hospital is vicariously liable for the negligent acts of its employees, including nurses who failed to escalate abnormal vital signs. Additionally, the Hospital failed to maintain adequate policies for the prompt evaluation of pediatric patients with fever and rash.

VII. DAMAGES

As a direct and proximate result of Defendants' negligence, Plaintiff and J.T.V. have suffered physical pain, mental anguish, disfigurement, impairment, medical expenses in the past and future, and loss of earning capacity. Plaintiff seeks damages within the jurisdictional limits of the Court, including exemplary damages for gross negligence.

VIII. MEDICAL EXPENSES

All medical expenses were reasonable and necessary for the treatment of J.T.V.'s injuries. Plaintiff itemizes these expenses and will present expert testimony regarding same.

IX. STATUTORY NOTICE

Plaintiff has complied with all statutory prerequisites, including providing notice under Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Section 74.101.

X. ATTORNEY'S FEES

Plaintiff requests recovery of reasonable attorney's fees as provided by law.

XI. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Plaintiff prays that citation issue and that upon final hearing, judgment be entered for Plaintiff against Defendants, jointly and severally, for actual damages, exemplary damages, costs, interest, and such other relief as the Court deems just.

Respectfully submitted,

GARZA & HENDERSON, LLP

By: ______________________________

Sarah M. Henderson
Texas Bar No. 24067890
1420 Willow Creek Lane
Houston, Texas 77008
Telephone: (713) 555-0142
Email: s.henderson@garzahenderson.com

ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

title: Plaintiff's Original Complaint and Jury Demand
text:
UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS

CAUSE NO. 4:24-CV-00123

ROBERTO I. GARCIA, PLAINTIFF,
v.

BAYLOR ST. LUKE'S HOSPITAL, INC., AND DR. ANITA M. CHEN, M.D., DEFENDANTS.

PLAINTIFF'S ORIGINAL COMPLAINT AND JURY DEMAND

COMES NOW, Roberto I. Garcia, Plaintiff, complaining of Defendants, and in support thereof alleges as follows:

1. This is a medical malpractice action arising out of negligent surgical care provided on February 14, 2023, at Baylor St. Luke's Hospital, Inc., located at 6720 Bertner Avenue, Houston, Texas 77030.

2. Plaintiff, Roberto I. Garcia, is a resident of Fort Bend County, Texas. He was born on March 14, 1971. His Social Security number is 457-89-1234.

3. Defendant Baylor St. Luke's Hospital, Inc., is a Texas corporation doing business in Harris County. Defendant Dr. Anita M. Chen, M.D., is a board-certified general surgeon, practicing at 1709 Dryden Road, Suite 1100, Houston, Texas 77030.

4. On February 14, 2023, Plaintiff underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed by Dr. Chen at Baylor St. Luke's Hospital. During the procedure, Dr. Chen inadvertently injured Plaintiff's common bile duct, causing bile leakage and subsequent peritonitis. Plaintiff required multiple revision surgeries and prolonged hospitalization.

5. Dr. Chen failed to recognize the injury during the initial operation, failed to convert to an open procedure when visualization was poor, and failed to obtain intraoperative cholangiography. These failures are below the accepted standard of care.

6. Baylor St. Luke's Hospital is liable under the doctrine of respondeat superior for the negligence of its employees, including nursing staff who failed to recognize signs of post-operative hemorrhage and infection.

7. As a direct result, Plaintiff has suffered severe pain, mental anguish, physical impairment, disfigurement, medical expenses, and lost wages. He continues to require medical care and treatment.

8. Plaintiff alleges gross negligence and seeks exemplary damages.

9. This Court has diversity jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1332 because Plaintiff is a citizen of Texas and Defendants are citizens of different states, and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

10. Venue is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1391.

11. Plaintiff demands trial by jury.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays for judgment against Defendants, jointly and severally, for all damages, costs, and such other relief as is just and proper.

Respectfully submitted,

THE LAW OFFICES OF CARTER & WHITFIELD, P.C.

Houston, Texas 77027

ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

Plaintiff demands a jury trial in this matter.

______________________

title: Defendants' Original Answer and Affirmative Defenses

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS

CAUSE NO. D-1-GN-24-004567

PAMELA SUE HAMILTON, PLAINTIFF,
v.

AUSTIN REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER, LLC, AND DR. MARCUS D. WEBSTER, M.D., DEFENDANTS.

DEFENDANTS' ORIGINAL ANSWER AND AFFIRMATIVE DEFENSES

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

NOW COME, Defendants Austin Regional Medical Center, LLC ("ARMC") and Dr. Marcus D. Webster, M.D. ("Dr. Webster"), and file this Answer, respectfully showing:

1. Defendants deny each and every allegation set forth in Plaintiff's Original Petition, except those expressly admitted herein.

2. Defendants admit that Plaintiff Pamela Sue Hamilton is a resident of Travis County, Texas, and that she was born on March 14, 1971. Defendants deny any negligence and assert that all care provided was within the standard of care.

3. Defendants assert the affirmative defense of comparative negligence, alleging that Plaintiff failed to follow post-operative instructions, failed to attend follow-up appointments, and otherwise contributed to her own injuries.

4. Defendants assert the affirmative defense of limitations, arguing that Plaintiff's claim is barred by the applicable statute of limitations under Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 74.251.

5. Defendants assert the affirmative defense of unavoidable accident.

6. Defendants assert the affirmative defense of sudden emergency.

7. Defendants assert that any injuries or damages were caused by pre-existing conditions unrelated to the care provided.

8. Defendants assert that any alleged damages are excessive and not supported by the evidence.

9. Defendants pray that Plaintiff take nothing, that costs be assessed against Plaintiff, and for such other relief as the Court deems just.

Respectfully submitted,

title: Plaintiff's Motion for Summary Judgment
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS

CAUSE NO. DC-24-09876

CYNTHIA LOUISE BAKER, PLAINTIFF,
v.

HEALTHTEXAS HOSPITAL, INC., D/B/A HEALTHTEXAS MEDICAL CENTER OF DALLAS, AND DR. GREGORY S. MITCHELL, M.D., DEFENDANTS.

PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT

COMES NOW, Cynthia Louise Baker, Plaintiff, and respectfully moves for summary judgment against Defendants on the issue of liability, and in support thereof shows:

I. INTRODUCTION

This is a medical negligence case arising from the failure to diagnose and treat a stroke in a 52-year-old woman. Plaintiff, born on March 14, 1971, presented to the emergency department on January 15, 2024, with acute onset of right-sided weakness, slurred speech, and facial droop. Despite clear indications of an acute ischemic stroke, Defendants failed to administer tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) within the recommended window, resulting in permanent neurological deficits.

II. UNDISPUTED MATERIAL FACTS

1. Plaintiff arrived at HealthTexas Medical Center of Dallas at 10:15 a.m. on January 15, 2024.

2. Dr. Gregory S. Mitchell, M.D., the emergency physician, evaluated Plaintiff at 10:30 a.m.

3. A CT scan was ordered and performed at 10:45 a.m.

4. The CT scan showed no hemorrhage, but Plaintiff's symptoms were consistent with large-vessel occlusion.

5. Dr. Mitchell did not consult a neurologist until 1:30 p.m., and tPA was not administered until 3:00 p.m., beyond the 4.5-hour window.

6. Expert reports conclude that timely intervention would have substantially reduced Plaintiff's injuries.

III. LEGAL ARGUMENT

Defendants owed Plaintiff a duty of care to provide timely and appropriate medical treatment. They breached that duty by failing to act within the standard of care. The causal link is established through expert testimony. Under Texas law, summary judgment is appropriate where no genuine issue of material fact exists.

IV. CONCLUSION

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests that this Court grant summary judgment on liability, set the matter for trial on damages, and award such other relief as is just.

Respectfully submitted,

PARKER & MOORE, LLP

By: ______________________________

Jessica R. Moore

ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

______________________
Jessica R. Moore

title: Notice of Appeal to the Fourteenth Court of Appeals

IN THE COURT OF APPEALS FOR THE FOURTEENTH DISTRICT OF TEXAS

APPEAL NO. 14-24-00567-CV

LARRY DEWAYNE JOHNSON, APPELLANT,
v.

SAN ANTONIO METHODIST HOSPITAL, INC., AND DR. KATHERINE A. FOSTER, M.D., APPELLEES.

NOTICE OF APPEAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUSTICES OF SAID COURT:

Appellant, Larry Dewayne Johnson, appeals from the final judgment entered on June 10, 2024, in Cause No. 2023-CI-12345, styled Larry Dewayne Johnson v. San Antonio Methodist Hospital, Inc. and Dr. Katherine A. Foster, M.D., in the 224th Judicial District Court of Bexar County, Texas, the Honorable Judge Martinez presiding.

This appeal is taken from an order granting summary judgment in favor of Appellees, which disposed of all claims. Appellant files this appeal within the time permitted by Texas Rule of Appellate Procedure 26.1(a).

Appellant is a resident of Bexar County, Texas, born on March 14, 1971. He asserts that the trial court erred in concluding that his claim was barred by the statute of limitations under Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 74.251, and further erred in excluding expert testimony that would have raised a genuine issue of material fact.

Appellant requests that the judgment be reversed and remanded. He submits that the trial court's interpretation of the statute is contrary to legal precedent, including cases such as Mitchell v. Smith, 123 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 2003, no pet.) and Johnson v. Baylor, 456 F.3d 789 (5th Cir. 2006). These authorities support the proposition that the limitations period may be tolled where the defendant's fraud conceals the injury.

Appellant further contends that the trial court improperly applied the Daubert standard, failing to allow a qualified physician to testify regarding causation.

The record on appeal has been requested. No transcript has yet been filed.

For these reasons, Appellant respectfully requests that this Court set the matter for briefing and ultimately reverse the trial court's judgment.

Respectfully submitted,

DELGADO & RAMIREZ, LLP
